key_insight: Increasing compressibility suppresses bluff-body oscillations during lock-in but amplifies them in the second desynchronized regime.
engineering_relevance: Mach-number effects on flow-induced vibration depend on the response regime, so compressibility cannot be assumed to uniformly stabilize bluff bodies.
method: Two-dimensional direct numerical simulations at free-stream Mach numbers 0.1–0.6.
Undamped transverse vibration of a circular cylinder at Re = 150 and rotary oscillation of an elliptic cylinder with aspect ratio 0.5 at Re = 200.
Comparison across the first desynchronized zone, synchronous lock-in branch, and second desynchronized zone.
evidence_signal: Both configurations show reduced amplitudes, fluctuating aerodynamic coefficients, and hysteretic jumps during lock-in, while amplitudes increase with Mach number in the second desynchronized zone following a modified Prandtl–Glauert relationship.
watch_item: Results are limited to two-dimensional, low-Reynolds-number simulations; persistence at higher Reynolds numbers remains unverified.
paper_title: Compressibility effects on the flow-induced motions of bluff bodies: common features from transverse and rotary oscillations
